title: Sweep the stale Node-oracle claims: Cargo.toml description, bee.mjs references, strangler and CUTOVER headers
action: Node tree is deleted (zero .mjs or .cjs files in the repo) but the code still claims otherwise. FIX: (1) crates/bee/Cargo.toml description (Rust port / strangler front door / delegates to node bee.mjs) -> describe what the binary IS now (the bee harness CLI). (2) rg for ANY .mjs reference across crates/bee/src — bee.mjs, guards.mjs, state.mjs, claims.mjs, worktree-holds.mjs and the rest (~40+ in devtools/skill_trees.rs, hooks/cli_shape.rs, verbs/reviews.rs, hooks/write_guard/paths.rs git-classification section provenance lines, others) — for each: if the comment explains CURRENT semantics, rewrite it to state the rule natively without citing the dead file; if it only narrates provenance or history, delete it. (3) CUTOVER headers (hooks/chain_nudge.rs, hooks/state_sync.rs, state.rs remnants after jp-2 and jp-4) — keep the behavioral contract text, drop the Node-is-gone migration narration. (4) strangler mentions in comments. (5) hooks/state_sync test fixture writes lib/worktree-holds.mjs as a vendored-module presence gate — check whether the production presence-gate still checks for a .mjs file that can never exist again; if it does, that gate is dead weight: simplify it and its fixture, keeping the test meaningful. DO NOT touch comments that merely use JS or JSON terminology correctly (e.g. notes explaining WHY a comparator keeps UTF-16 code-unit order, or that a behavior models JS undefined via Option). This cell depends on all prior cells so it sweeps final text, not text about to be deleted.
verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml green from the worktree; rg for bee.mjs and strangler in crates/bee/src returns zero production-comment hits

truths: Cargo.toml description no longer claims Node delegation
zero bee.mjs references left in crates/bee/src except any a locked decision explicitly kept
vendored-mjs presence gates are either live-justified or removed with their fixtures
